title: I keep reverting back to Notes
body:
I like the idea of ToDoist. I’ve had it on my phone for over a year or so. It sits in a widget on my Home Screen. But there are a few reasons why I stop using it time again and revert back to Notes.

One, I find visualising sequences of planned work over the immediate time horizon hard. I know there is a calendar view but that’s not how I work, my mind is focused on a rolling 5 sometimes 7 days into the future outlook. I plan the tasks day by day and the set out to achieve them. Expecting to shuffle items about as the days go on.

Two, updating deadlines is cumbersome. Commonly, if I set goals for today that I don’t achieve I want to be able to move them to tomorrow without picking dates from a calendar. Then I want to shift tomorrow’s tasks back a day and so on in a cascading update. Picking dates takes a lot of precise taps to get right and if you make a mistake it’s a hassle to fix. 

Three, I would like to be able to see the recent tasks achieved as well when reviewing future tasks to do. Momentum of task achievement is hard to see when tasks are removed from a list. I understand one can view completed tasks, but I want to view the last eg 3 or 5 days tasks completed not the entire history of tasks. I will propose how to present this below.

I would like a new view to plan and work with tasks ie n-day in the future and m-days into the past, view of tasks that rolls day by day. This would allow the user to see the tasks achieved and planned in one view. 

I’d like to be able drag any tasks planned from the day prior or past to the next day and then shift other items along ideally using a tap, hold and drag action.

You see the reason why I stop using this app is partly because of the friction involved with updating dates for tasks not completed via the calendar picker. When there are many tasks to update, maintaining this app becomes a massive chore in itself - and that makes me revert back to Notes.

title: Lifechanging! Thank you.
body:
This app has changed my life. I could never stick at diaries, calendars, or task lists because they either didn’t give me the fidelity and control I wanted, or had too much and were too tedious to use and add tasks and events efficiently. Plus lists inside lists inside lists make me cringe. I wanted to be able to get an overview of everything very quickly. Nothing worked how I wanted it too, and nothing stuck. So I resigned myself to the fact that I would be hopelessly and irreparably disorganised forever, doomed to a lifetime of being late, forgetting events and/or the things I needed to take to them, even while being surrounded by a million productivity apps, sites, and gurus.
Then one magical day a Jeff Su (shoutout) YouTube video popped up randomly in my feed, and featured a 30-second highlight of Todoist as one tool in a productivity/task tracking workflow. Something about the interface triggered hope in me, and having downloaded and used it for 5 minutes, it was love at first sight. The Boards! They were things of beauty. The text recognition for dates and times, genius. It was like someone had looked inside my brain and made an app for the way I thought and visualised. I will be a subscriber and evangelist forever. My whole life is slowly but surely being loaded into this app and I am still only scraping the surface of its functionality. The new Calendar view is an endgame, it was the only major feature I had wished Todoist had when I first subscribed. My only fear is that it may one day be turned off. To Amir and the entire Doist and Todoist team, thank you from the bottom of my heart.

title: Finally, an app that works
body:
For decades, I have been struggling to get myself organised; I have tried system after system to organise my projects, list and monitor my tasks and try to reach a level of productivity that gets close to matching what I want but with no success. Each one starts strong but quickly fades away as I get swamped by urgent activities, with the system getting ignored and rapidly falling into disuse. 
But Todoist is different. The simple yet highly structured interface lets me organise and cascade projects, easily add, schedule and monitor tasks and keep notes and comments in one place to stay on top of progress. I have only been using it for just over a week but it has revolutionised the way I organise my days and has massively increased my ability to stay on top of multiple projects at the one time. I had no hesitation purchasing a Pro subscription and have no doubt that I will be using Todoist for a long time.

title: Todoist beats them all. And I've bought and tried them all.
body:
Since moving to todoist I'm actioning and closing all my tasks way faster than before and I'm a veteran of task management GTD (getting things done) and all that stuff.

I migrated from my Omnifocus to Todoist and in fact built a fit-gap to help with migration and love todoist.

My history includes all sorts of software so I've used them all - toodledo etc and even built my own on Microsoft xRM platform with all finer details like Eisenhower quadrant etc but Todoist beats them all because of the increased productivity and integrations via Zapier etc to harvest slack projectmanager smartsheet office365 google calendars emails etc. And not to mention how well it integrated to my smartwatch smartphones different OSs Windows Mac Wunderlist (where I work with my EA) etc etc.

I found out about todoist from a co-worker at a new company I joined.

I have left everything else now, Asana, Trello, BaseCamp, and many other tools that were tying my processes together.

One of the biggest advantage is how well it's not where I spend loads of time in but just doing all my tasks so quickly that I almost spend less amount on actual todoist itself but in past I would spend a huge effort inside my task management tools just planning but less doing. Now it's opposite. Everything auto plans the way I like it and the natural English converting dates etc I now see how powerful that is when todoist reads my emails and calendars and always automatically understands dates and times.

1 unexpected surprise for me was how well the location nearby feature works. I was driving and was near a shopping centre and it told me about things I needed to get because I was around that place. In past all other task management software I used didn't work this smoothly and immediately with nearby location feature that well.

I cannot over stress the integrations feature how everything flows in and out of my todoist to other tools in my life. Just the ability to integrate to all other cloud based systems itself is worth 1000 times the price of Todoist. 

If no other reason, I am completing a whopping amount of tasks everyday now in a short span of time that I'm actual left free and wondering what to do with new found spare time. It makes me feel like I haven't even done much today when in fact I'm doing 3-4times the number of tasks I used to do. Even things I don't like doing (eat the frog) I now am doing and not skipping. I'm not breaking any good habits that were hard to form in other apps. And yet I feel my productivity will even double to 6-8 times from my previous time and task management workflows.

All thumbs up!

After trying many task management apps, this is the one which fits perfectly my needs. I use large commercial PM systems but this one fills the gap. I use it for all those operational daily tasks which - for the sake of keeping large project plans simple - do not find their place in complex systems.
Also great for consulting jobs and BAU activities. You need to think well how to structure your system. I use Work/Private at the top level and then Projects, using then labels for distinctive groups - 4 progress labels, 5 type of task label (eg financial, reporting etc), 5 type of ownership labels (eg vendors, internal business groups, PM). Ability to use custom query for filters is excellent feature. Exportable reporting in Excel format is something which would add additional value.

I could go on with the pros and cons but overall it's a great 2do manager with some very helpful features.
